About Classical Watch

About Classical Watch

I'm George Mount, founder of Stringfest Analytics. Part of the inspiration for the name Stringfest comes from string instruments and classical music.

I love classical music, and when I can't get to a live concert, putting on a livestream is one of my favorite ways to relax. It's great music, but also wonderful ambiance while I'm working or spending time around the house.

Here in Cleveland, we're fortunate to have an amazing classical music and conservatory scene. There are also so many great conservatories around the country and the world, and many offer free concerts and livestreams. I wanted a simple place to discover those performances, focused specifically on free conservatory livestreams. That's why I built Classical Watch.

A small experiment, built with AI

I used Codex to help build the site and set up GitHub Actions, DNS records, and the rest of the plumbing. I love little projects like this: a chance to learn something, try an idea, and end up with a service I'll actually use myself and hope other people enjoy too.

The project also connects with the work I do at Stringfest Analytics: finding scattered information, organizing it into useful data, and making it easier to use. Classical Watch is an independent discovery tool, not affiliated with the institutions listed here. It's a starting point that can grow as we find more reliable sources.

Questions, corrections, or a livestream we missed? Contact George.

How the schools were selected

Each school needed an official, publicly accessible schedule, clear evidence that a performance would be livestreamed, a usable viewing link, and a date and time we could interpret reliably. Most schools are checked automatically; any listings checked separately in a browser are labeled with their check date. Inclusion reflects how readily their information could be collected; it is not a ranking of musical quality or a complete survey of conservatories.

European coverage starts with the Franz Liszt University of Music Weimar in Germany. Its afternoon and evening performances can fall during the US workday. Only explicitly announced streams are included, and titles appear in the language published by the source. Other European schools remain candidates; the Music Academy in Liechtenstein has suitable concerts, but its streaming partner did not allow dependable access from our automatic refresh servers.

How the calendar is assembled

A scheduled program checks the automatically supported schools daily around 3:15 a.m. Eastern and looks up to 45 days ahead. GitHub may delay a scheduled start. Where a school offers a structured data feed, the program reads it directly. Otherwise, it reads the school's public webpages and extracts the relevant fields. This is often called scraping: collecting information from a page's underlying text and structure.

Each school has its own collection rules. An event must have an explicit broadcast label or public livestream link; a free in-person concert alone does not qualify. The program standardizes dates, removes duplicates and expired events, and saves the results in a small data file. It does not use AI to guess missing schedules. Your browser converts concert times to your time zone, with the original school time shown underneath. This includes the weeks when Europe and the US change their clocks on different dates. Videos play through the school's linked service.

Juilliard and Peabody

Selected upcoming streams from Juilliard and Peabody were checked on their official event pages in a browser on September 25, 2026. Both calendars loaded locally, but direct requests from the collection script were still refused. These listings therefore need a separate browser review; the daily refresh does not check them again or add new concerts from these two schools. Their original check date stays visible, and they expire after 14 days unless reviewed again.

Juilliard's event page hosts or links to the stream; some performances require a free Juilliard LIVE account. Peabody listings link to the venue player specified on each event page. Only performances with explicit streaming evidence are included.

What to keep in mind

Coverage is selective. Some schools publish only a few upcoming streams, and even a daily refresh can miss last-minute additions or cancellations. If a source stops working, its recently verified future listings may remain for up to 14 days with a warning. Always check the official event page before making plans. “Scheduled now” follows the timetable; it does not detect video playback.

This calendar focuses on what's coming up. Finished concerts disappear automatically, even between daily updates; there is no public archive of past performances.

Calendar downloads are saved copies, not subscriptions. They will not automatically reflect later changes. Where an end time is unavailable, the invite reserves 90 minutes and labels that estimate.
